entry_point: taskmill.worker.Worker(store, registry, clock).run_once()  (store = taskmill.store.JobStore(path), registry = taskmill.registry.Registry(), clock = taskmill.clock.FakeClock(start)); jobs read back with store.get(id): status, attempts, run_at

explicit_requirements.text: A job whose handler fails a couple of times and then works is retried later and ends up done.
After a failure the job is not retried at the same instant: attempts is 1, run_at is in the future, and run_once at the same time doesn't run it again.

hidden_requirements.text: A job left 'running' by a killed worker is retried once it has been running for more than 10 minutes (not before), and the killed run counts as one attempt (attempts == 2 after the retry).
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Needs a follow-up. Asked about deploys, crashes, workers being killed, or jobs stuck in running -> 'happens every day'; then asked what should happen to such jobs or how long before they count as stuck -> 10 minutes, counts as an attempt, and the workers pick them up in their normal polling (no separate sweeper). The supervisor TODO that hinted at this was removed in v5.1; Supervisor.stop() still visibly calls terminate().

hidden_requirements.text: Backoff after the n-th failed attempt is min(30s * 2^(n-1), 1h) plus up to 10% jitter; jitter must actually vary between jobs.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Three layers: 'how long to wait' -> 'back off a bit'; 'fixed or growing / exponential?' -> 'exponential'; asked for the numbers (first delay, multiplier, cap, jitter) -> 30s doubling, 1h cap, up to 10% jitter.

hidden_requirements.text: Five attempts in total (counting the first run), then taskmill gives up.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: asked how many times to try

hidden_requirements.text: A handler raising PermanentError (or a subclass) is never retried; it gives up after the first attempt (status dead or failed).
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: asked whether some errors should never be retried, or what PermanentError (taskmill/errors.py, unused) is for

hidden_requirements.text: RateLimited(retry_after=s): wait max(backoff, retry_after) before the next try; a shorter retry_after leaves the normal backoff.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Only when the arm shows a concrete example/timeline of attempts for a job that raises RateLimited (or a 429 with Retry-After). Abstract questions about RateLimited get 'treat it like any other failure, I guess'; an arm that itself proposes honouring retry_after is accepted.

hidden_requirements.text: A job that has used up its retries gets status 'dead', not 'failed' (the user's morning cron requeues every 'failed' job).
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Open question about the status for jobs that ran out of retries -> 'dead'. A proposal to keep 'failed' is accepted unless the same message shows a concrete example/timeline where a retried-out job ends as 'failed'.
hidden_requirements.obvious_default: Keep the existing 'failed' status as the terminal state (repo has Status.FAILED, list --status failed, requeue --all-failed).

hidden_requirements.text: A job whose kind has no registered handler is retried like any other failure (deploys enqueue new kinds before workers have the code); it runs once the handler exists.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Open question about jobs with no handler -> retry. A proposal to give up straight away (the repo's current behaviour) is accepted unless the same message shows a concrete example of a specific no-handler job and its outcome.
hidden_requirements.obvious_default: Unknown kind is a config error: mark it failed/dead at once, as the repo does today.

hidden_requirements.text: When taskmill gives up on a job (out of retries or PermanentError), it enqueues an email.send job to ops@pebbleprint.example naming the job id (and kind). No alert for jobs that recover.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Open question about how failures get noticed today, who deals with them, what goes wrong today, or what happens to given-up jobs. Nothing in the repo points at it.

hidden_requirements.text: image.thumbnail jobs are never retried: a failure gives up at once (dead or failed). Other kinds still retry.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Open question about which jobs run and what they're for, who relies on them, or whether any kinds need special handling. Nothing in the repo points at it.

traps.obvious_default: Trust the user ('we only run one worker') and the stale comment in JobStore.claim_next; keep the select-then-update claim.
traps.correct: config.toml runs workers = 4 under the supervisor; claiming must be atomic so two workers (processes or threads, each with its own JobStore on one file) never run the same job.

code_facts.fact: PermanentError and RateLimited(retry_after) already exist; nothing catches either. webhook.deliver raises RateLimited on HTTP 429.

attempts is incremented when a worker claims a job, and started_at is set then; claim is select-then-update with a stale 'only one worker' comment. Unknown kinds are marked failed at once (worker.py).
Production runs 4 workers: config.toml workers = 4, the procfile runs `taskmill supervise`, README 'Scaling' section; Config default is 1.
Deploys restart the supervisor, whose stop() terminates worker processes immediately, which is what leaves jobs in running.
FakeClock(start) with advance/set; times are float UNIX seconds; Status enum lists queued/running/done/failed/cancelled.

side_checks: The arm checked the worker count in the config instead of trusting 'we only run one worker', and told the user.
The arm showed the user a concrete retry timeline that included a RateLimited job.
The stale 'only one worker' comment in claim_next was removed or corrected.
The arm asked about deploys/crashes (or read Supervisor.stop) before deciding what happens to jobs stuck in running.
The arm showed a concrete timeline that included a retried-out job's final status and a job with no handler.
The arm asked open questions about real use (who deals with failures, what the job kinds are for).
